newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina does not want fresh IMF money - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentina does not want fresh IMF money - paper.

text.p: Argentina and International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials will begin negotiating Monday a program which will leave Argentina under Fund supervision until 2000 but will not include specific new loans, a newspaper reported.

Under the deal, the government will commit itself to completing its stalled program of changes to make labor rules more flexible as well as to reforming its health and justice systems, according to the Clarin daily, which quoted unnamed Economy Ministry negotiators.
The IMF also wants Argentina to agree to shifting its tax base to place more emphasis on income tax and less on wealth, land and payroll taxes.

Argentina hopes a new three-year, Extended Fund Facility accord including IMF technical supervision would reassure investors by guaranteeing a smooth transition of power after presidential elections in 1999.
The IMF team, headed by Chilean Tomas Raichman, is due to stay in Argentina for 10 days.
